index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the conceptual differences in multi-turn input formatting across three approaches: HiTrans (Li et al., 2020a), EmoBERTa (Kim and Vossen, 2021), and TED (the proposed method). The global layout is structured vertically, with each method presented as a separate horizontal sequence of tokens, aligned under labeled headings. At the top, a legend defines token types: B (BOS, Begin-of-Sequence, shown as blue square), E (EOS, End-of-Sequence, white square), S (SEP, Separator, pink square), P (SPEAKER, yellow square), and T (TURN, gray square). A 'Token' is represented as a white square, and a 'Turn' is indicated by a bracketed group of tokens.

The first row, labeled 'Single-turn input', shows a simple sequence: one B token followed by three empty tokens and ending with an E token, representing a basic input format.

The second row, 'HiTrans (Li et al., 2020a)', depicts a multi-turn input where each turn begins with a B token and ends with an E token at the final turn. Intermediate turns are separated by ellipses, indicating multiple turns, but no explicit speaker or turn markers are used beyond the B tokens.

The third row, 'EmoBERTa (Kim and Vossen, 2021)', introduces speaker-aware formatting. It starts with B followed by P (SPEAKER), then proceeds through multiple turns marked by alternating P and S (SEP) tokens. Each turn is implicitly bounded by P tokens, with S tokens separating speaker segments within a turn.

The fourth row, 'TED (Our proposal)', presents the proposed method. It begins with B, followed by tokens representing the first turn, then a T (TURN) token. Subsequent turns are marked by T tokens, with S (SEP) tokens inserted between turns to denote transitions. The sequence ends with E. Below this sequence, arrows indicate priority weights: β¹ points from the first turn to the current turn (βᶜ), βᶜ⁻¹ points backward from the current turn to the previous turn, βᶜ⁺¹ points forward to the next turn, and βᵐ points toward the end of the sequence. These weights reflect the model's ability to assign different importance levels based on turn position and speaker information, as emphasized by the caption: 'Priority according to turn position and speaker information'.

Visually, all tokens are squares with black borders; B is blue, E is white, P is yellow, S is pink, and T is gray. The sequences are horizontally aligned, with ellipses (...) indicating omitted intermediate tokens. Brackets below certain segments label them as 'Turn'. The connections are represented by black arrows with arrowheads, pointing from one turn segment to another, annotated with β superscripts to denote priority coefficients. The overall structure emphasizes how TED enhances multi-turn modeling by explicitly marking turns and incorporating dynamic weighting based on temporal and speaker context.
